note: SET-A settlement capability schema (MIN_A_ARCHITECTURE.md section 9), first used by MIN-D for mining (Mining spec section 3: levels 1-4 are the owner's progression; level 5 is a proposal and is not here). A settlement's level in an industry is derived, never stored as truth: Discovery.evaluate recomputes it each dawn from the village's real assets (living villagers' jobs and skills, tools held by villagers, households and the manor's yard, deposits, stations, portals, structures, the manor's discovery records). It is the highest level whose needs, and every lower level's, all hold; it falls when one stops holding (the spec's 'can regress'). The player's own goods and skills are not the settlement's. Need kinds: deposit_access {level}; practitioners {jobs?, skill?, min_level?, count}; tool_stock {tool, count}; transport {any: handcart | carry}; station {type, count}; records {what: discovery, count}; portal {min_depth}; structure {what, count} (pit ramps and timber supports are built by MIN-E/MIN-F: none exist yet, so levels 3 and 4 cannot hold). The needs are agent decisions after the spec's 'evidence required in world' column.
